title: Run the study again: sampling distributions and standard error

objectives.statement: Explain why a repeat of a study on a fresh sample of the same size returns a different mean, and describe the distribution the repeat means would form, naming what its centre estimates and what its spread measures.

Estimate the standard error of a sample mean from a reported sample standard deviation and sample size, state its unit, and distinguish a precision band around the reported mean from the distribution of a fresh independent mean.
Predict how the standard error of a mean changes when the sample size is multiplied by a stated factor, and calculate the sample size needed to reach a stated target standard error.

Distinguish a standard deviation from a standard error by stating which quantity each describes, select the one a given sentence requires, and diagnose the effect on a reader when a report swaps them or leaves the label off.

State what the central limit theorem licenses about the sampling distribution of a mean, and judge from a described population and sample size whether reading a normal band off that distribution is defensible.
